assessed_by: source reading of the break site; no differential run (structurally impossible -- see below)
why_not_a_case: The break site cannot fail a test, for two independent reasons. It is unreachable from a test, and even when it fires the exception is swallowed.

blocking_reasons.detail: The adaptation is inside `private void loadWebForms()`, called only from the private FormManager() constructor, which is reached only via FormManager.getInstance(). loadWebForms() immediately calls WorkgroupManager.getInstance() and iterates its workgroups, reading each one's `jive.webform.wg` property out of the Openfire database. Standing that up means standing up an Openfire server instance, not a unit test.

The fromXML call sits inside `try { ... } catch (Exception e) { Log.error(e.getMessage(), e); }`. ForbiddenClassException is therefore logged and execution continues -- the workgroup form silently fails to load. Even with a live server, the break produces a log line and a missing form, never a test failure. There is no assertion a differential could hang on.

library.note: The parent already declares 1.4.20; the 1.4.16 -> 1.4.18 crossing that verify_traversal confirmed is 22 commits earlier, and a later bump took it to 1.4.20.

why_the_signature_is_causally_clean: The commit message names the cause outright: "FormManager,java load workgroupForm: xstream have Type limit.must set allowTypes when xstream update 1.4.20". The fix allows exactly the two types loadWebForms deserializes (WorkgroupForm, FormElement). This is an upgrade-triggered adaptation beyond reasonable doubt -- it simply cannot be demonstrated by a build.

observations_worth_recording.bundled_unrelated_changes: The commit carries three unrelated changes: the xstream allowTypes fix (FormManager), a dispatcher-ordering change (WorkgroupUtils, moving getBuiltInDispatcherClasses() to the end so custom dispatchers take precedence), and a null-guard on getChatBot() (Request). Only the first is the adaptation. A commit-level classifier that assumed one commit means one intent would mis-summarise this.
observations_worth_recording.incomplete_fix: The adaptation adds allowTypes to loadWebForms() but NOT to getDataForm(), 14 lines earlier in the same file, which also calls `xstream.fromXML(form)` on a bare `new XStream()`. So getDataForm remains broken at 1.4.20. Interesting as data about how clients respond under time pressure -- they fix the path that visibly hurt them, not every instance of the pattern.

rules_assessment.1_differential_run: FAIL -- structurally impossible, this is the rule it fails
rules_assessment.4_client_adaptation_to_the_break: PASS -- commit message names the upgrade explicitly

precedent: Filed the same way as xstream-spark: causally real, production, boundary-crossing, but not standalone-verifiable. Kept because it is evidence about the break's reach and about how clients adapt, but it is not a verified case and must not be counted as one.
